text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- European Commission to make new decision on Kesko-Tuko merger by January. Comissioner Karel van Miert says daily goods market competition status quo in Finland before Kesko's acquistion of Tuko should be restored by summer.
- Finland joins the race to head the World Intellectual Property Organisation, Wipon. Candidate selection process is on.
- Holding a doctorate degree does not necessarily guarantee a job. Only 20 per cent of Finnish employers would employ a Ph.D holder on the merit of the degree alone, study shows.
- Swedish telecommunications group Ericsson receives this year's Finnish quality award.
- Shares on Helsinki OTC- and Brokers' list have risen steadily this autumn as investors seek small companies with favourable growth prospects.

- The government will in the next few weeks pass new legislation on the Bank of Finland to parliament. Proposal expected to set more precise guidelines for the central bank's responsibilities and competence.
- President Martti Ahtisaari says corporate sector should take more responsibility for employment.
- Co-operative banking group OKOBANK's central association Osuuspankkien Keskusliitto (OKL) will decide on new group structure and rules on January 8.
- Five consortiums made tenders to build new highway between Jarvenpaa and Lahti. Among companies in the consortiums are Swedish Skanska and NCC, and Finnish YIT-yhtyma, Lemminkainen and Neste.
- President Martti Ahtisaari calls for restructuring of welfare state to meet needs of next century, saying state can no longer carry all social welfare responsibilities.
- Many retailers in the Pirkamaa area express cautious satisfaction with the EU's rejection of Kesko-Tuko merger.
